candidates.title: Manual's /dev/cmio section says the host returns the next request type in the yield's DATA field; the emulator, libcmt and the manual's own HTIF section put it in REASON (DATA carries the length)
candidates.component: Manual doc/README.md ('The /dev/cmio device'), which specifies the guest-visible yield interface that the emulator's send_cmio_response implements and that machine-guest-tools libcmt decodes
candidates.role: The manual is the specification (THREAT_MODEL preamble). The behavior it describes is produced by input delivery (honest operator: 'input delivery') and consumed by guest software (libcmt, machine-guest-tools v0.18.1-test1)
candidates.location: doc/README.md lines ~7250-7258 ('The reasons paired with HTIF_YIELD_CMD_MANUAL are HTIF_YIELD_MANUAL_REASON_RX_ACCEPTED (... the host sets the `data` field on resume to HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE or HTIF_YIELD_REASON_INSPECT_STATE to indicate the type of the freshly loaded input ...)'). Contradicted by doc/README.md ~7664-7668 (HTIF Yield: 'The REASON field in fromhost carries the request type, and the DATA field carries the request length in bytes') and ~7780-7800 (host loop: 'Write HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE to REASON and length as DATA in fromhost'), and by the code: src/send-cmio-response.cpp send_cmio_response ('yieldData = (reason & mask16) << 32 | (dataLength & mask32); writeHtifFromhost'), the regenerated SendCmioResponse.sol (same), and libcmt io.c unpack() (reason = bits 47..32, data = bits 31..0) / rollup.c accepted() ('*n = req->data; return req->reason;') and cmt_rollup_finish ('next_request_type = reason; next_request_payload_length = me->fromhost_data').
candidates.description: On resume from an rx-accepted (or, after the host's revert, rx-rejected) manual yield, the emulator writes fromhost = (request type << 32) | input length, i.e. REASON = HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE (0) or INSPECT_STATE (1) and DATA = the input's byte length (for an InputBox input, 292..65536). The /dev/cmio section of the manual, which is the section aimed at 'tooling that needs to talk to the device directly', states the opposite: that the host sets the `data` field to the request type. A guest or binding written against that section reads the input length (>= 292 for any InputBox input) as the request type, so it never recognizes an advance-state request (0) and, per the manual's own guest loop ('Else length = 0, reason = RX_REJECTED'), would reject every input; it also has no source for the payload length. The manual is internally inconsistent on the reason/length encoding of the yield interface, which R7 lists as an area where 'a correct guest relies on the architecture for ... data integrity'. No code path is wrong: the emulator, both verifiers, libcmt and the other two manual sections agree.
candidates.trigger: No adversary action needed: any author of a guest binding or tool that follows the manual's /dev/cmio section. Every input (chosen by any sender) then reaches that guest with DATA = length and REASON = 0.
candidates.reachability: Every advance-state delivery to a machine at an rx-accepted manual yield writes this fromhost value (send_cmio_response, all paths). Confirmed by code reading of the three emulator paths and libcmt; the emulator/verifier encoding was also exercised in the experiment below (fromhost write is part of every logged delivery that verified).
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? The trigger is a guest following the manual, not an excluded condition; 'An application that is not correctly designed' is excluded only for what the application gets, but here the question is whether the specification itself is defective, so not excluded on its face. 2 Role: the defect is in the manual, the specification; the behavior is input delivery (honest operator) and guest software (libcmt). Section 8: 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' 3 High/Medium cases: 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on' does not fit, because R7 says a correct guest relies on 'The rx buffer, the tx buffer, and the yield interface (contents, lengths, and reason encoding)'. 4 Critical reading: if the /dev/cmio sentence were right, every path of input delivery would deviate from the documented yield interface in reason encoding, an R7 deviation ('In these areas, any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest, even a deviation that is consistent across all paths'), which section 8 would rate Critical. 5 Low reading: the manual's HTIF section and host loop, which are the normative register-level description, match the code; under that reading the /dev/cmio sentence is a documentation defect that violates no rule, rated Low ('a real defect that violates no rule'). Deciding fact: which manual section is normative for the yield interface. I claim Low, with Critical only under the literal reading of the contradiction clause.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (Critical under the literal 'as if the manual were right' reading applied to the /dev/cmio section alone; triage should decide which section is normative)
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not change any hash or proof. It threatens the goal only through guest software: a binding built from the manual's /dev/cmio description misreads every input's type and length and so deviates from the rollup interface on every input, making an otherwise correctly designed application reject everything; that application's outputs would then not reflect its inputs. It also violates the requirement that the manual specify the yield interface unambiguously (R7 is defined against 'the devices as the manual documents them').
candidates.evidence: Code reading: src/send-cmio-response.cpp, bugs/harness/work/solidity-step/regenerated-patched/src/SendCmioResponse.sol, src/htif-address-range.cpp (manual-yield ack sets fromhost = DEV_YIELD|CMD_MANUAL, then delivery overwrites it with reason<<32|length), libcmt io.c/rollup.c at v0.18.1-test1 (cloned to the scratch dir). Differential experiment /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r2/DFINPUT/lengths.lua: native send, log + C++ verify and the regenerated Solidity sendCmioResponse (EVM harness) agree on the after-hash for input lengths 1, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 65, 255-257, 292, 4096, 4097, 65535-65537, 2^20+1, 2^21-1, 2^21 and 2^21+1 (the last a no-op on all three), so the fromhost encoding is the same on every path.
candidates.test_idea: Load the valid-template (Linux + guest-tools rootfs) or baremetal-template, deliver an advance input of length L (e.g. 300 bytes), and assert that the resulting htif_fromhost satisfies the encoding stated in every manual section: HTIF_REASON_FIELD(fromhost) == HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE and HTIF_DATA_FIELD(fromhost) == L (HTIF section) AND HTIF_DATA_FIELD(fromhost) == HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE (/dev/cmio section). The test exits 1 today because the two cannot both hold; it passes once the /dev/cmio section is corrected (the test is then rewritten to grep the manual for the corrected statement), so in practice the fix is to the manual and the test can assert that doc/README.md's /dev/cmio section no longer says the host sets the `data` field to the request type.

not_covered: Linux cmio kernel driver between libcmt and HTIF (out of scope); libcmt's unpack of the ioctl result was taken as the guest-visible encoding.

No run of the real InputBox -> DaveConsensus.provideMerkleRootOfInput -> CartesiStateTransition path on the released chain; Dave's input Merkle root convention (ceilLog2, min 5, zero padding) was checked by reading LibBinaryMerkleTree/LibKeccak256/LibMath only, and the EVM experiment used the harness data_hash, not Dave's library.

Nothing was run inside a Cartesi Machine for the guest tools: libcmt (io.c, rollup.c, abi.c, buf.c), the rollup CLI (rollup.cpp) and rollup-http-server (http_service.rs, rollup/mod.rs, main.rs, dapp_process.rs) were reviewed by reading only; no Rust build, no fuzzing of cmt_abi_* with arbitrary rx contents (InputBox inputs are canonical EvmAdvance encodings, so only canonical decoding was reasoned).
Inspect-state delivery (outside verified history) was not followed.

cartesi.evmu event decoding was read for dynamic bytes (length/padding bounds) but not fuzzed; prt-ethereum abi:event/topics matching (address case normalization of appContract) was not checked beyond the PRT demo settling.
JSON-RPC client/server send/log/verify_send_cmio_response were read (oversized data replaced by rx_len+1 zero bytes, which keeps the no-op), but not run remotely.
Gas and calldata limits of the maximum-size delivery proof (left to the A3/R12 angles; round 1 measured 94,180 bytes).
The PRT player's computation-hash leaves around a delivery (begin_input, epoch_stopped inputs, revert tails) beyond the input bytes themselves.

The in-memory retention of every input's bytes by prt-epoch.lua/prt-bridge.lua for the open and sealed epochs was noted but judged allowed by R12 ('its total grows only with the inputs ... of the epochs still open'); not reported.

The yield utility's help text (and the manual's copy of it) lists reasons 'tx-voucher' and 'tx-notice' that yield.c does not accept ('tx-output' is accepted instead): a diagnostic-tool defect, not on the input path, not reported.
